item.title: How Scholarly Research Comes to Matter for Industry and Society: Research Impact as an Innovation Challenge
item.content:encoded:
Yat Ming Ooi, University of Auckland

Tzameret Rubin, Oxford Brookes University

Nuran Acur, University of Glasgow

Sebastian Fixson, Babson College

Paavo Ritala, LUT University

This special issue examines research impact as an innovation management challenge rather than solely a measurement problem. While abundant research is produced across social sciences, humanities, and professions, translating this research into practice and societal benefit remains limited. The issue develops a process-oriented understanding of how scholarly research creates and sustains impact in practice, examining mechanisms and dynamics often overlooked by outcome-focused grand challenges scholarship or measurement-oriented evaluation literature.

Current approaches address either what impact is or how to measure it, but not how research actually gets taken up and applied. This issue aims to identify the processes through which impact unfolds, examining intermediary roles, temporality, conditions for use, and engaged scholarship. By treating impact as a manageable process rather than only a countable outcome, the field can better resource, sequence, and improve the pathways through which research reaches practice and society.

Appel publié par R and D Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Problem framings and relationships shaping research impact
  • Alignment, trust, and agenda setting preceding impact
  • Identification of impactful research questions
  • Research translation and transformation across boundaries
  • Roles of intermediaries, brokers, and boundary spanners
  • Research refusal and rejection at point of use
  • Conditions for impact embedding, endurance, decay, and reversal
  • Feedback loops and lags in impact trajectories
  • Experimentation and iterative testing in impact achievement
  • Power asymmetries in co-production
  • Institutional arrangements shaping research influence
  • Organizational capabilities and enabling conditions for impact
  • Reshaping incentives and evaluation frameworks through process view
  • Managing for impact deliberately
